messages.author: e46f1261377a98d2
messages.subject: predict factor scores from CFA
parts:
dear lavaan communtiy,

I have a very basic question. 

I had used the function predict() to predict factor scores from a CFA analysis. 

Then, I computed descriptive statistic of the predicted factor scores, and the mean is close to 0, and sd is close to 1. 

¿Is that means factor scores are standardized?  ¿Is there any other way to obtain factor scores?

thank you in advance!

A.

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: predict factor scores from CFA
parts:
The mean and variance of a latent variable are arbitrary because they
are, definitionally, not measured on any scale. There are some common
options for setting the scaling.

What does your cfa() call look like? If you set std.lv = TRUE in your
function call, then you should expect a mean of about 0 and an SD of
about 1 in the factor scores (where the "true" latent has exactly 0
and 1).

Dear Patrick

Thank you very much for your answer. I appreciate it very much!

I did set std.lv=T in the function call. But now I tried setting std.lv=F, and then compute the decription of the factors again, and the mean is equall to 0, but the sd is not equall to 1, though it  is in the range 0-1 instead. 

My functions are the following: 

# the model 

m1<- 'TCN=~b13+b26+b37
MES=~b36+b49+b54
INF=~b9+b23+b53
HCS=~b6+b20+b31
SDT=~b14+b27+b38
MOL=~b8+b22+b45
COF=~b2+b4+b16+b18+b29
VIC=~b1+b7+b12
HAP=~b5+b19+b43
EPE=~b17+b30+b39
INS=~b3+b24+b40
social=~TCN+MES+INF+HCS
personal=~SDT+MOL+COF'

m1<-cfa(m1, data=CFA, std.lv=T, estimator="MLM")
summary(m1, fit.measures=T)

## factor scores prediction 

predict(m1)
scores_m1<-predict(m1)
scoresm1_df<-data.frame(scores_m1)
describe(scoresm1_df)

Question is: 

If I set std.lv=T in the fuction call, I should expect factor prediction scores with mean 0 and sd 1? Can I say factor scores are standardized? 

I am asking this because a reviewer required me to present the descriptive statistics (mean, sd, range) of the factor loadings. So, I want to be sure to report that factors scores are standardized or not. 

Moreover, I am keen to know what are the options for setting the scaling. Would you be kind to give a hint on this?

Thank you so much!

A.

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: predict factor scores from CFA
parts:
The most common other option to set the scaling is a unit (1.00)
loading to one of the indicators. lavaan, like most SEM software,
defaults to the first indicator. So if you look at your unstandardized
results without std.lv=T, you will probably see a loading of 1.00 for
b13 on TCN, for b36 for MES, etc.

You haven't changed how you're scaling the mean (default in a
single-group model is factor means constrained to zero), so it's still
zero, but the variance will differ depending on the indicator with the
fixed loading. That's why for many purposes std.lv=T is more
convenient for a CFA (it can get a bit messier for SEM).

But factor scores are impure reflections of factors, so even though
the *factor* has M=0 SD=1 (i.e., is standardized), the observed factor
scores will not be exactly M=0 SD=1, though they should be in the
ballpark.

Pat
